title: MATH GAOKAO - 1
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Roster Notation for Positive Even Integers
questions.learningObjective: Represent a described set of positive even integers less than \(10\) in roster notation.
questions.question: Which of the following is the roster form of the set of positive even integers less than \(10\)?
questions.explanation: The positive even integers less than \(10\) are \(2,4,6,8\). The number \(10\) is not less than \(10\), so it is excluded. Therefore the roster form is \(\{2,4,6,8\}\).
questions.hint: List positive even integers and remember that “less than \(10\)” excludes \(10\) itself.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a set given in set-builder notation over the integers into roster form.
questions.question: The set \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -2<x<3\}\) in roster form is:
questions.explanation: The integers satisfying \(-2<x<3\) are strictly greater than \(-2\) and strictly less than \(3\). These are \(-1,0,1,2\). The endpoint \(3\) is not included because the inequality is \(x<3\). Hence \(A=\{-1,0,1,2\}\).
questions.hint: List the integers between \(-2\) and \(3\), remembering that both endpoints are excluded.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether two sets given in different notations are equal.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb N^+\mid x^2<10\}\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: For \(B\), the positive integers \(x\) satisfying \(x^2<10\) are \(x=1,2,3\), since \(1^2=1\), \(2^2=4\), \(3^2=9\), and \(4^2=16\ge 10\). Thus \(B=\{1,2,3\}\). Therefore \(A=B\).
questions.hint: Find all positive integers whose squares are less than \(10\), then compare the resulting set with \(A\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the formula for the number of subsets of a finite set.
questions.question: How many subsets does the set \(S=\{a,b,c,d\}\) have?
questions.explanation: A set with \(n\) elements has \(2^n\) subsets. Since \(S\) has \(4\) elements, the number of subsets is \(2^4=16\). This includes the empty set and \(S\) itself.
questions.hint: Use the formula for the number of subsets of a set with \(n\) elements.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a given number belongs to a set defined by an inequality over the integers.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -3\le x<4\}\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The set \(A\) consists of integers from \(-3\) up to but not including \(4\). Thus \(A=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}\). Therefore \(-3\in A\), while \(4\notin A\).
questions.hint: List all integers satisfying the inequality, paying attention to whether each endpoint is included.

questions.learningObjective: Translate a verbal description of a real interval into set-builder notation.
questions.question: Which set-builder notation describes all real numbers greater than \(-2\) and at most \(5\)?
questions.explanation: “Greater than \(-2\)” means \(-2<x\), so \(-2\) is excluded. “At most \(5\)” means \(x\le 5\), so \(5\) is included. Therefore the correct set-builder notation is \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid -2<x\le 5\}\).
questions.hint: Match each phrase to its inequality symbol: “greater than” excludes the endpoint, while “at most” includes it.

questions.learningObjective: Find the complement of a finite set relative to a given universal set.
questions.question: Let \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) and \(A=\{2,4,6\}\). The complement of \(A\) in \(U\) is:
questions.explanation: The complement \(A^c\) consists of all elements of the universal set \(U\) that are not in \(A\). Removing \(2,4,6\) from \(U=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) leaves \(\{1,3,5\}\). Hence \(A^c=\{1,3,5\}\).
questions.hint: Start with all elements of \(U\) and remove every element that belongs to \(A\).

questions.learningObjective: Represent a set of real numbers defined by a simple inequality using interval notation.
questions.question: Which interval represents the set \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid x<3\}\)?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(x<3\) means \(x\) can be any real number less than \(3\), but \(3\) itself is not included. In interval notation, this is written as \((-\infty,3)\). The bracket \(]\) would incorrectly include \(3\).
questions.hint: Recall how parentheses and brackets indicate whether an endpoint is excluded or included.

questions.concept: Intersection and Cardinality from Set Notation
questions.learningObjective: Convert two sets from set-builder notation to roster form and determine the cardinality of their intersection.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb N^+\mid x\le 4\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -2<x<2\}\). How many elements are in \(A\cap B\)?
questions.explanation: \(A=\{1,2,3,4\}\). For \(B\), the integers strictly between \(-2\) and \(2\) are \(-1,0,1\), so \(B=\{-1,0,1\}\). The common elements are \(\{1\}\), so \(A\cap B=\{1\}\). Therefore \(A\cap B\) has \(1\) element.
questions.hint: Write both sets in roster form, then identify their common elements.
